blocks.content: The service conditions of a member shall not be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.

rows: Same procedure as Supreme Court Judge

items: Note the vital difference in retirement ages: Supreme Court Judges retire at 65 years, while High Court Judges retire at 62 years.
Expenditure 'charged upon' the Consolidated Fund of India can be discussed in Parliament but is not subject to vote.
Members of the UPSC and State PSCs are ineligible for further employment under the Government of India or a State after retirement, except specific allowed appointments.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Constitutional functionaries such as the CAG, CEC, and UPSC members hold office for a fixed term of 6 years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Salaries, allowances, and pensions of constitutional post-holders are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India and are non-votable by Parliament.
Service conditions cannot be varied to the disadvantage of an incumbent after their appointment, safeguarding administrative independence.
Security of tenure ensures that constitutional authorities cannot be removed at the pleasure of the executive, requiring specific parliamentary procedures for removal.
